newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia accepts joint probe on tanker disaster.
newsitem.headline: Russia accepts joint probe on tanker disaster.

text.p: Moscow has agreed to the creation of a joint Russia-Japanese commission to find out what caused the Russian tanker Nakhodka to sink causing widespread pollution off the Japanese coast, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Tass said in a report issued on Thursday night that Transport Minister Nikolai Tsakh had agreed to a request from Tokyo for cooperation in investigating the sinking on January 2.

It quoted Tsakh as saying Tokyo remained convinced that the disaster was caused by a combination of stormy weather and the advanced age of the tanker, which was launched over 25 years ago. Moscow believed the Nakhodka broke up after hitting an unidentified object in the water.
Tsekh said he would provide Japanese authorities with its loading inventory and technical assessments of the Nakhodka's structural condition.
The loss of the Nakhodka caused some of the worst pollution seen off the Japanese coast and affected important fishing areas.
